subproblems.title: Integer median of an integer-valued function on the unit cube (Simon 6.5.1 (31), (35); parent steps 1–2)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} ⊆ Euclid (m + 1) and Lⁿ := volume. Let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ take an integer value at every point (u(y) ∈ ℤ for all y) and be integrable on Q₁. Then there is β ∈ ℤ such that Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {y : β ≤ u(y)}) ≥ 1/2 and Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {y : u(y) ≤ β}) ≥ 1/2 (measures in [0, ∞]) and |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → ∃ β : ℤ, 1 / 2 ≤ volume ({y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} ∩ {y | (β : ℝ) ≤ u y}) ∧ 1 / 2 ≤ volume ({y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} ∩ {y | u y ≤ (β : ℝ)}) ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1 and 2, i.e. the choice (31) of the integer β_F and the bound (35) in Simon's proof of the Deformation Theorem (Ch. 6, 5.1; chapter-06.txt). Notation: n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, Lⁿ := volume on Euclid n, μ := Lⁿ⌞Q₁ (volume.restrict Q₁).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) Q₁ is open (a finite intersection of the open sets {y : 0 < y_i} and {y : y_i < 1}; the coordinate maps y ↦ y_i are continuous), hence Borel.
 (b) Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1. The coordinate map y ↦ (y_0, …, y_m) (WithLp.ofLp) is a measure-preserving bijection from Euclid n onto ℝ^{Fin n} with the product Lebesgue measure (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp; inverse PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). It maps Q₁ onto the box ∏_i (0, 1) = Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo 0 1), whose measure is ∏_i (1 − 0) = 1 (Real.volume_pi_Ioo).
 (c) Measurable representative. u is integrable on Q₁, so it is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ. Fix a Borel function ũ with u = ũ μ-almost everywhere. The set Z := Q₁ ∩ {u ≠ ũ} is Lⁿ-null (Q₁ is measurable, so μ-null subsets of Q₁ are Lⁿ-null). Hence for every Borel set B ⊆ ℝ the sets Q₁ ∩ u⁻¹(B) and Q₁ ∩ ũ⁻¹(B) differ only inside Z. So Q₁ ∩ u⁻¹(B) is Lⁿ-null-measurable and has the same Lⁿ-measure as the Borel set Q₁ ∩ ũ⁻¹(B). This applies in particular to A_b := Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ b} and to Q₁ ∩ {b ≤ u}, for b ∈ ℝ.

1. The distribution function. For b ∈ ℤ put F(b) := Lⁿ(A_b) ∈ [0, 1]. F is nondecreasing, since A_b ⊆ A_{b'} for b ≤ b'.
 – F(N) → 1 as N → ∞ (N ∈ ℕ). Indeed, the sets A_N increase, and their union is Q₁ because u is real-valued. Continuity of measure from below (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop) gives F(N) → Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1. Since 1/2 < 1, there is N₁ ∈ ℕ with F(N₁) > 1/2.
 – F(−N) → 0 as N → ∞. The sets A_{−N} decrease, are null-measurable, have finite measure (≤ 1), and have empty intersection. Continuity from above (tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop) gives F(−N) → 0. Hence there is N₀ ∈ ℕ with F(−N₀) < 1/2. By monotonicity, F(b) < 1/2 for every integer b ≤ −N₀.

2. Choice of β (Simon (31)). The set S := {b ∈ ℤ : F(b) ≥ 1/2} contains N₁. Every element of S is > −N₀, so S is bounded below. Let β be its least element (Int.exists_least_of_bdd, or csInf_mem in ℤ). Then F(β) ≥ 1/2 and, as β − 1 ∉ S, F(β − 1) < 1/2.

3. Two-sided median property.
 – First, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) = F(β) ≥ 1/2.
 – Second, u is integer-valued. So for every y, β ≤ u(y) holds iff u(y) ≤ β − 1 fails: if u(y) = z ∈ ℤ, then β ≤ z ⟺ ¬(z ≤ β − 1). Hence Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u} = Q₁ ∖ A_{β−1}. The set A_{β−1} ⊆ Q₁ is null-measurable with finite measure, so (measure_diff) Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u}) = Lⁿ(Q₁) − F(β − 1) = 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2 ≥ 1/2.

4. The bound |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u| (Simon (35)). Both functions below are integrable on Q₁.
 – β = 0. The claim is 0 ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|, which is true.
 – β > 0. For μ-a.e. y (namely y ∈ Q₁ ∖ Z) we have |u(y)| ≥ β·1_{β ≤ ũ}(y). Indeed, if β ≤ ũ(y) = u(y) then |u(y)| ≥ u(y) ≥ β, and otherwise |u(y)| ≥ 0. Integrating over Q₁ gives ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ β·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ ũ}) = β·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u}) ≥ β/2, by 0(c) and step 3.
 – β < 0. Likewise |u(y)| ≥ −u(y) ≥ −β = |β| on Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}. So ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β|·Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ |β|/2.
In every case |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

Steps 3 and 4 give the three conclusions for this β. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1 via the measure-preserving coordinate map; a Borel representative ũ makes the level sets of u null-measurable with the same measures.
F(b) = Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ b}) is nondecreasing with F → 1 at +∞ and F → 0 at −∞ (continuity of measure).
β := least integer with F(β) ≥ 1/2; integrality gives Q₁ ∩ {β ≤ u} = Q₁ ∖ {u ≤ β − 1}, of measure 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2.
Integrating |u| ≥ |β| over the half-measure set {β ≤ u} (β > 0) or {u ≤ β} (β < 0) gives |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

subproblems.title: Deviation from a θ-median is controlled by the double-integral oscillation (Simon Ch. 2, 2.7; parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ Euclid P measurable with L(W) := volume(W) < ∞, v : Euclid P → ℝ integrable on W, β ∈ ℝ and θ > 0 with θ·L(W) ≤ L(W ∩ {β ≤ v}) and θ·L(W) ≤ L(W ∩ {v ≤ β}) (real numbers via toReal). Then ∫_W |v − β| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)·L(W)⁻¹·∫_W ∫_W |v(x) − v(y)| dy dx, where 0⁻¹ := 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (v : Euclid P → ℝ) (β θ : ℝ), MeasurableSet W → volume W ≠ ∞ → IntegrableOn v W → 0 < θ → θ * (volume W).toReal ≤ (volume (W ∩ {y | β ≤ v y})).toReal → θ * (volume W).toReal ≤ (volume (W ∩ {y | v y ≤ β})).toReal → ∫ y in W, |v y - β| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹) * ((volume W).toReal)⁻¹ * ∫ x in W, ∫ y in W, |v x - v y|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3. Its first line is ∫_Q|v − v̄| ≤ Lⁿ(Q)⁻¹∫_Q∫_Q|v(x) − v(y)|. Its 'Consequently' paragraph replaces the mean v̄ by a θ-median β' with factor 1 + θ⁻¹ (Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.7, condition (∗)). Both hold for any integrable v; this child is the combination of the two. Notation: |W| := volume(W).toReal ∈ [0, ∞), and all integrals are over subsets of W.

0. Degenerate case. If |W| = 0, then volume(W) = 0 (it is finite), so the restricted measure volume⌞W is zero and every integral over W vanishes. Both sides are then 0; the right side has the factor ∫_W(…) = 0. Assume |W| > 0 from now on, and put v̄ := |W|⁻¹∫_W v.

1. Integrability.
 – For each fixed x, y ↦ |v(x) − v(y)| is integrable on W: it is a.e.-strongly measurable and bounded by |v(x)| + |v(y)|, and constants are integrable on W because volume(W) < ∞.
 – The function (x, y) ↦ |v(x) − v(y)| is integrable on W × W for (volume⌞W) ⊗ (volume⌞W). It is a.e.-strongly measurable (compose v with the two projections: AEStronglyMeasurable.fst/snd) and bounded by |v(x)| + |v(y)|, which is integrable for the finite product measure.
 – Hence (Fubini, Integrable.integral_prod_left) the function x ↦ ∫_W|v(x) − v(y)| dy is integrable on W.
 – Likewise x ↦ |v(x) − v̄| and x ↦ |v(x) − β| are integrable on W.

2. Mean step (the Jensen step of parent step 3). For x ∈ W, linearity of the integral gives v(x) − v̄ = |W|⁻¹∫_W (v(x) − v(y)) dy. Hence |v(x) − v̄| ≤ |W|⁻¹∫_W|v(x) − v(y)| dy. Integrate over W and use step 1 (integral_mono):
 (∗) ∫_W|v − v̄| ≤ |W|⁻¹∫_W∫_W|v(x) − v(y)| dy dx.

3. Median replacement (parent step 3, 'Consequently'). Let ṽ be a Borel function with v = ṽ a.e. on W. The sets W ∩ {β ≤ v} and W ∩ {β ≤ ṽ} differ by a null set, so they have the same measure; the same holds for W ∩ {v ≤ β} and W ∩ {ṽ ≤ β}.
 – Case β ≥ v̄. On the measurable set E₊ := W ∩ {β ≤ ṽ} we have, a.e., |v − v̄| ≥ v − v̄ ≥ β − v̄ ≥ 0. Hence (β − v̄)·volume(E₊).toReal ≤ ∫_{E₊}|v − v̄| ≤ ∫_W|v − v̄|. Here volume(E₊).toReal = volume(W ∩ {β ≤ v}).toReal ≥ θ|W| by hypothesis, and β − v̄ ≥ 0. So (β − v̄)θ|W| ≤ ∫_W|v − v̄|, i.e. |β − v̄|·|W| ≤ θ⁻¹∫_W|v − v̄|.
 – Case β < v̄. Use E₋ := W ∩ {ṽ ≤ β}: there |v − v̄| ≥ v̄ − v ≥ v̄ − β > 0 a.e. With the second hypothesis this gives the same inequality |β − v̄|·|W| ≤ θ⁻¹∫_W|v − v̄|.

4. Conclusion. Pointwise |v − β| ≤ |v − v̄| + |v̄ − β|. Integrating over W:
 ∫_W|v − β| ≤ ∫_W|v − v̄| + |v̄ − β|·|W|
  ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)∫_W|v − v̄| (step 3)
  ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)·|W|⁻¹·∫_W∫_W|v(x) − v(y)| dy dx (step 2, (∗)). ∎
proof_key_steps: If volume(W) = 0 both sides vanish; otherwise put v̄ := |W|⁻¹∫_W v and check integrability of all integrands (Fubini for the partial integral).
Jensen step: |v(x) − v̄| ≤ |W|⁻¹∫_W|v(x) − v(y)|dy, integrated over W.
θ-median step: on {β ≤ v} (if β ≥ v̄) or {v ≤ β} (if β < v̄) one has |v − v̄| ≥ |β − v̄|, so |β − v̄||W| ≤ θ⁻¹∫_W|v − v̄|.
Triangle inequality: ∫_W|v − β| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)∫_W|v − v̄| ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)|W|⁻¹∫∫|v(x) − v(y)|.

subproblems.title: Fubini identity for mixed points on the cube Q_δ (the Fubini step of parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, δ ∈ ℝ, k ∈ Fin (m + 1), Q_δ := {y ∈ Euclid (m + 1) : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i}, and let h : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ be integrable on Q_δ. For x, y let a_k(x, y) be the point whose j-th coordinate is y_j for j < k and x_j for j ≥ k. Then ∫_{Q_δ} ∫_{Q_δ} h(a_k(x, y)) dy dx = volume(Q_δ)·∫_{Q_δ} h.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (δ : ℝ) (k : Fin (m + 1)) (h : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), IntegrableOn h {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ} → ∫ x in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, h (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => if j < k then y j else x j)) = (volume {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}).toReal * ∫ x in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, δ < y i ∧ y i < 1 - δ}, h x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3: 'Integrating over x, y ∈ Q (Fubini) bounds the i-th term'. The integrand h(a_k(x, y)) does not involve the variables x_j (j < k) or y_j (j ≥ k). Integrating them out gives the factor volume(Q_δ). This is that Fubini step, made precise by a coordinate swap. Notation: E := Euclid (m + 1), n := m + 1, μ := volume on E, Q := Q_δ.

1. The swap σ. Define σ : E × E → E × E by σ(x, y) := (a_k(x, y), c_k(x, y)), where c_k(x, y) has j-th coordinate x_j for j < k and y_j for j ≥ k. Thus σ exchanges the j-th coordinates of x and y for every j < k and fixes all other coordinates. Clearly σ(σ(p)) = p for all p. So σ is a bijection that is its own inverse, and (being measurable, step 2) a measurable equivalence; in particular it is a measurable embedding.

2. σ preserves μ ⊗ μ.
 – The coordinate map WithLp.ofLp : E → ℝ^{Fin n} preserves volume (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), and so does its inverse WithLp.toLp (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). Taking products (MeasurePreserving.prod), it suffices to show that τ(x, y) := ((j ↦ y_j if j < k else x_j), (j ↦ x_j if j < k else y_j)) preserves volume ⊗ volume on (ℝ^{Fin n})².
 – Identify (ℝ^{Fin n})² with (ℝ × ℝ)^{Fin n}: the identification (MeasurableEquiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow) maps the product measure ∏_j (L¹ ⊗ L¹) to (∏_j L¹) ⊗ (∏_j L¹) (measurePreserving_arrowProdEquivProdArrow).
 – In these coordinates τ acts factorwise: by the swap (s, t) ↦ (t, s) on the j-th factor ℝ × ℝ when j < k, and by the identity when j ≥ k. Each factor map preserves L¹ ⊗ L¹ (Measure.measurePreserving_swap; MeasurePreserving.id). So the factorwise map preserves the product measure (measurePreserving_pi).
 – Composing these measure-preserving maps shows that τ, and hence σ, is measure preserving.

3. σ⁻¹(Q × Q) = Q × Q. Q is the product of the same interval (δ, 1 − δ) in every coordinate. σ only exchanges coordinates between the two factors, so σ(x, y) ∈ Q × Q iff every coordinate of x and of y lies in (δ, 1 − δ), i.e. iff (x, y) ∈ Q × Q. Consequently σ preserves the restricted measure (μ ⊗ μ)⌞(Q × Q) (MeasurePreserving.restrict_preimage_emb). This measure equals (μ⌞Q) ⊗ (μ⌞Q) (Measure.prod_restrict).

4. Integrability.
 – Q is bounded (|y_i| ≤ |δ| + |1 − δ| for every coordinate), so volume(Q) < ∞ and μ⌞Q is a finite measure.
 – Since h is integrable for μ⌞Q, the function (x, y) ↦ h(x) is integrable for (μ⌞Q) ⊗ (μ⌞Q) (Integrable.comp_fst).
 – Since σ preserves this measure and is a measurable embedding (MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb), (x, y) ↦ h(σ(x, y)₁) = h(a_k(x, y)) is integrable as well.

5. Computation.
 ∫_Q ∫_Q h(a_k(x, y)) dy dx
  = ∫_{Q×Q} h(σ(x, y)₁) d((μ⌞Q) ⊗ (μ⌞Q)) (Fubini, integral_prod, step 4)
  = ∫_{Q×Q} h(x) d((μ⌞Q) ⊗ (μ⌞Q))(x, y) (measure preservation, MeasurePreserving.integral_comp, step 3)

 – Writing h = Σ_i h_i e_i: ⟨F(y), h⟩ = Σ_i h_i·Dw(y)e_i = Dw(y)h for all h.
 – Hence InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E (F(y)) = Dw(y), and since the Riesz map is an isometry, |F(y)| = ‖Dw(y)‖.
 – F is C^∞. w is C^∞, so y ↦ Dw(y) is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right). Each component y ↦ Dw(y)e_i is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply). The coordinate equivalence (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Fin P → ℝ)).symm is continuous linear (contDiff_pi).

 – g is C^∞: |F|² = ⟨F, F⟩ is C^∞ (ContDiff.inner); |F|² + ε² ≥ ε² > 0, so its square root is C^∞ (ContDiff.sqrt) and nonvanishing; products and quotients by nonvanishing C^∞ functions are C^∞.

0. Dη is continuous (η is C¹) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport η. Hence Dη has compact support and |Dη| ≤ C for some C ≥ 0.
1. Oddness. Differentiating η(−y) = η(y) by the chain rule gives Dη(−y) = −Dη(y).
2. Derivative of η∗u. u is integrable, hence locally integrable, and η is C¹ with compact support. So D(η∗u)(x) = (Dη∗u)(x) = ∫Dη(x − z)u(z)dz (HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left, convolution_eq_swap). Evaluation at s(x) commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply). So D(η∗u)(x)(s(x)) = ∫Dη(x − z)(s(x))u(z)dz.
3. Divergence of η∗s. Likewise D(η∗s)(z) = ∫A_{z,x}dx with A_{z,x}(w) := Dη(z − x)(w)s(x). The trace is a continuous linear functional on the finite-dimensional space of linear maps, so it commutes with the integral. The rank-one map A_{z,x} has trace Dη(z − x)(s(x)) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). So div(η∗s)(z) = ∫Dη(z − x)(s(x))dx.
4. Fubini. H(x, z) := Dη(x − z)(s(x))u(z) is a.e.-strongly measurable on the product and satisfies |H| ≤ C|s(x)||u(z)|, which is integrable (Integrable.mul_prod). So H is integrable and ∫_x∫_z H = ∫_z∫_x H (integral_integral_swap).
5. By step 2 the left side of step 4 is ∫D(η∗u)(x)(s(x))dx. By step 1, Dη(x − z) = −Dη(z − x), so by step 3 ∫_x H(x, z)dx = −u(z)·div(η∗s)(z). Hence ∫D(η∗u)(x)(s(x))dx = −∫u(z)·div(η∗s)(z)dz. ∎

Source: parent proof, step 5 (Simon Ch. 2, 2.5): for a C^∞ g with compact support in W and |g| ≤ 1, ∫Du_ε·g = −∫u_ε div g = −∫u div(φ_ε∗g) ≤ V. Dependencies: sibling smooth_duality (Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_cp_smooth_duality) and sibling mollifier_adjoint (Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_sp_mollifier_adjoint).
Notation: E := Euclid (m + 1), ũ := 1_{Q₁}u (Set.indicator Q₁ u), u_η := convolution η ũ (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, so u_η(x) = ∫η(t)ũ(x − t)dt; div G := trace DG.

1. Smoothness. Q₁ is open (a finite intersection of open coordinate half-spaces), hence measurable. So ũ is integrable on E (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator), hence locally integrable. η is C^∞ with compact support, so u_η is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left). This is the first conclusion.

2. The domain W := Q_δ is open (a finite intersection of open coordinate half-spaces). It is bounded: since δ > 0, Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ ⊆ closedBall(0, √(m + 1)).

3. Reduction. By the sibling smooth_duality (P := m + 1, w := u_η, which is C^∞ by step 1, and W := Q_δ, open and bounded by step 2), it suffices to prove: ∫Du_η(x)(g(x))dx ≤ V for every C^∞ g : E → E with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q_δ and |g| ≤ 1. Fix such a g.

4. The mollified field G := convolution η g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, G(x) = ∫η(t)g(x − t)dt, is admissible for (H):
 (a) G is C^∞: g is continuous, hence locally integrable; apply HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left.
 (b) G has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution).
 (c) tsupport G ⊆ Q₁.
  – support G ⊆ support η + support g (support_convolution_subset) ⊆ tsupport η + tsupport g.
  – tsupport η + tsupport g is compact (a sum of compact sets), hence closed, so tsupport G ⊆ tsupport η + tsupport g.
  – Here tsupport η ⊆ closure B(0, δ) ⊆ closedBall(0, δ) and tsupport g ⊆ Q_δ.
  – If x = z + q with |z| ≤ δ and q ∈ Q_δ, then for every i, |z_i| ≤ |z| ≤ δ. So x_i = q_i + z_i > δ − δ = 0 and x_i < (1 − δ) + δ = 1, i.e. x ∈ Q₁.

 ∫Du_η(x)(g(x))dx = −∫ũ(z)·div G(z)dz = −∫_{Q₁} u·div G.
 The last equality holds because ũ(z)·div G(z) = 1_{Q₁}(z)·u(z)·div G(z) (integral_indicator).

6. Apply (H) to −G (admissible by step 4): ∫_{Q₁} u·div(−G) ≤ V. Now D(−G) = −DG (fderiv_neg) and the trace is linear, so div(−G) = −div G and ∫_{Q₁}u·div(−G) = −∫_{Q₁}u·div G. With step 5, ∫Du_η(x)(g(x))dx = −∫_{Q₁}u·div G ≤ V.

G = η∗g is C^∞, compactly supported, |G| ≤ 1 and tsupport G ⊆ closedBall(0, δ) + tsupport g ⊆ Q₁.

This yields the same limit inequality as the parent's L¹-convergence argument; the mean form ∫_W|u − ū| ≤ n·s·V of the parent follows from it by the Jensen step of the sibling median_deviation.

1. Mollified functions. For each k, the sibling mollified_variation (hypotheses: u integrable on Q₁, (H), δ > 0, and the stated properties of η_k) gives: v_k is C^∞ and ∫_Q‖Dv_k‖ ≤ V.

2. Smooth Poincaré for v_k. v_k is C^∞, hence C¹, and 0 ≤ δ < 1/2. So the sibling smooth_poincare gives
 D_k := ∫_Q∫_Q|v_k(x) − v_k(y)| dy dx ≤ C·∫_Q‖Dv_k‖ ≤ C·V,

 – Since δ > 0, Q ⊆ Q₁, so ũ = u on Q.

 – f(x, y) ≤ |u(x)| + |u(y)|. u is integrable on Q ⊆ Q₁ and μ is finite, so f is integrable for μ ⊗ μ; its a.e.-strong measurability comes from AEStronglyMeasurable.fst/snd.

Source: parent proof, step 4 (as in Simon's printed proof of Ch. 2, 2.7: 'choose convex W ⊂⊂ U such that ∫_U|u − β| ≤ 2∫_W|u − β| … for example W = {x ∈ U : dist(x, ∂U) > δ}'). We must choose δ ∈ (0, 1/4] with Lⁿ(Q₁ ∖ Q_δ) ≤ 1/4 and ∫_{Q₁∖Q_δ}|f| ≤ ½∫_{Q₁}|f|, using continuity of measure and of the integral. With Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ the latter is equivalent to ∫_{Q₁}|f| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|f|. In the parent this is applied to f = u − β. Notation: L := volume on Euclid (m + 1).

1. Basic facts.
 – Q₁ and every Q_δ are open (finite intersections of open coordinate half-spaces), hence measurable.
 – L(Q₁) = 1: the coordinate map WithLp.ofLp is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) and maps Q₁ onto the box ∏(0, 1), of measure 1 (Real.volume_pi_Ioo).
 – For δ ≥ 0, Q_δ ⊆ Q₁, hence L(Q_δ) ≤ 1.

2. Exhaustion. Put δ_j := 1/(j + 4) for j ∈ ℕ, so 0 < δ_j ≤ 1/4 and δ_j decreases to 0.
 – The sets Q_{δ_j} increase with j.
 – ⋃_j Q_{δ_j} = Q₁. If y ∈ Q₁ then r := min_i min(y_i, 1 − y_i) > 0 (finitely many coordinates), and y ∈ Q_{δ_j} as soon as δ_j < r.

3. Measure of the boundary layer. The sets Q₁ ∖ Q_{δ_j} are measurable and decreasing, have empty intersection (step 2), and have finite measure (≤ 1). By continuity from above (tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop), L(Q₁ ∖ Q_{δ_j}) → 0. Choose j₁ with L(Q₁ ∖ Q_{δ_j}) ≤ 1/4 for all j ≥ j₁ (the sequence is nonincreasing).

4. Integral. |f| is integrable on Q₁ = ⋃_j Q_{δ_j}, an increasing union of measurable sets. So ∫_{Q_{δ_j}}|f| → ∫_{Q₁}|f| (tendsto_setIntegral_of_monotone).
 – If ∫_{Q₁}|f| = 0, every δ satisfies ∫_{Q₁}|f| = 0 ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|f|; put j₂ := 0.
 – Otherwise ∫_{Q₁}|f| > ½∫_{Q₁}|f|, so there is j₂ with ∫_{Q_{δ_j}}|f| ≥ ½∫_{Q₁}|f| for all j ≥ j₂ (the sequence is nondecreasing).

5. Take j := max(j₁, j₂) and δ := δ_j. Then 0 < δ ≤ 1/4, L(Q_δ) ≤ 1 (step 1), L(Q₁ ∖ Q_δ) ≤ 1/4 (step 3) and ∫_{Q₁}|f| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|f| (step 4). ∎

Q_{1/(j+4)} increases to Q₁.
